transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-05
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood Solutions), Daniel Ortega (CTO, Brightpath), Maya Singh (Lead ML Eng, Brightpath), Shawn Reeves (Security), Rita Alvarez (PM)

Summary:
Brief review of last week's pilot metrics; focused discussion on which model versions to pin for traffic and how to implement a version-gate + failover playbook. Agreed to additional latency sweeps and a short failover runbook. Action items and next steps captured.

Topics:
- Model catalog comparison (v2.1 vs v2.0-quant vs v1.9)
- Soft fallback vs hard rollback strategies
- Version gating thresholds (p95 latency, error rate, hallucination regression)
- Security checks for private deployment (KMS, SAML, audit logs)

Action items (quick): Marcus to run latency sweep; Maya to share prompt set; Lena to share pricing; Shawn to confirm KMS events.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Lena (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, we should be able to keep this to under an hour, um, quick check — did everyone get the model perf deck i emailed?
[00:00:12] Daniel (Brightpath CTO): yep, got it. skimmed. overall nice work. i know we had some higher p95s on longer contexts though.
[00:00:20] Marcus (Redwood SE): yeah so to recap quickly, last week's run had three variants: v2.1 (baseline, fp16), v2.0-quant (4-bit q4-ish), and v1.9 (older gen). we saw median latency around 48ms for short prompts, but p95 jumped to ~1.1s on 2k tokens for v2.1. the quant variant had lower cost but p95 was closer to 1.4s in some buckets.
[00:00:45] Maya (Brightpath): that aligns with what we saw in staging. the main product flow is sensitive to 300-500ms spikes. anything over 800ms creates poor UX. so we need strict gating for p95.
[00:00:58] Lena: agreed. question for you daniel and maya — what's the primary metric that would force a rollback for you? latency thresholds? error rate? semantic degradation?
[00:01:10] Daniel: top priority is correctness; hallucination regression beyond current baseline is a showstopper. latency matters, but we can tolerate brief spikes if accuracy holds.
[00:01:20] Rita (PM): and from a product POV we want to avoid user-visible drops; so if visible error rate > baseline + 1.5%, that should trigger a pause.
[00:01:30] Shawn (Security): also we need to ensure any version change doesn't alter logging/audit coverage — audit events must be captured consistently and keys handled by our KMS.
[00:01:40] Marcus: noted. on the rollback gating i'd propose a three-tier policy: 1) pre-gate (canary small %, automated checks against eval set), 2) soft fallback (route slow or degraded calls to a cheaper older but compatible flavor), 3) hard rollback (pin all traffic back to previous version and notify).
[00:01:58] Maya: when you say "soft fallback" do you mean per-request routing based on latency and quality signals?
[00:02:06] Marcus: yes, exactly. Redwood runtime can do request-level routing based on policy — e.g., if inference p50/p95 breaches threshold, route new requests to a lower-latency pinned variant, while continuing to shadow or log responses for analysis. small note, sometimes the telemetry tag gets mis-placed — we saw a few events labeled as "reedwood" in the logs last week — not a blocker but will clean up.
[00:02:26] Lena: ha, yeah the autocorrect on the logs.
[00:02:30] Daniel: can you describe how the canary gating works? we want to avoid a canary that passes on simple prompts but fails on complex clinical ones.
[00:02:38] Marcus: good point. we recommend canary checks use a weighted eval set: 70% representative short flows, 30% heavy-context and clinical prompts that you provide. Maya if you can share 100 canonical prompts we'll fold them in.
[00:02:50] Maya: yes i'll share those later today.
[00:02:53] [00:15:00] Marcus: walking through the perf CSV — note that v2.0-quant reduces token cost by ~37% but cost per 1k tokens for real traffic depends on batching. with continuous batching enabled we saw better amortization, but that increases tail latency in some cases.
[00:15:20] Rita: so is it better to tune batching on the runtime or on the client side?
[00:15:26] Marcus: runtime-level batching lets us optimize across requests, but you can control max batch latency. for Brightpath's low-latency requirement I'd suggest conservative batch windows (e.g., 5ms) and prefer prefix caching for common completions to reduce repeated attention work.
[00:15:40] Daniel: how does that interact with KV cache for chat sessions? our sessions are medical annotation, so consistency is important.
[00:15:47] Marcus: KV cache is per-session and safe; it actually reduces compute for repeated context. we just need to ensure cache eviction policy fits your session lengths. sometimes we saw cache thrash for very long sessions; we can increase TTL or pin certain keys.
[00:16:00] Shawn: on the security front — the private deployment image you provided, how are we handling secrets? are we forcing HSM-backed keys?
[00:16:07] Priya (Redwood Solutions): we support both KMS and HSM integrations; for Brightpath we recommended HSM for root keys and KMS for per-tenant envelopes. we'll document the exact audit events (key usage, rotation, access) and share.
[00:16:22] Shawn: and SSO/SAML? we need SCIM and group sync so permissions map to AD groups.
[00:16:28] Lena: yep that's on the security checklist we sent. we'll also map RBAC roles to groups.
[00:16:33] [00:30:00] Marcus: circling back to the failover playbook — here's a proposed sequence: 1) Canary: 1% traffic for 30 minutes; automatically run checks against eval set and telemetry for p95, error-rate, hallucination score. 2) If canary breaches minor thresholds, switch to soft-fallback: route 30% of traffic to pinned older variant (v1.9) and shadow to v2.1 for offline analysis. 3) If soft-fallback makes things stable, gradually roll forward; if not, hard rollback to v1.9 and open incident.
[00:30:30] Daniel: timeframe for canary check — is 30 minutes enough? what about diurnal patterns?
[00:30:38] Marcus: depends on traffic volume. if you have low qps, 30 min might not give enough samples; we can gate on absolute sample counts instead (e.g., min 500 canary requests).
[00:30:48] Maya: can we have an escape hatch? e.g., manual switch to hard rollback via console/CLI and an API webhook to our PagerDuty?
[00:30:55] Lena: yes, we'll surface a single-click rollback and webhook integration; Marcus will wire the webhook.
[00:31:02] [00:40:00] Marcus: quick demo of the console routing policy — shows live traffic, can create a version-gate rule with p95 > 800ms or hallucination metric > 1.5% then action to soft-fallback. note: hallucination metric is evaluated with your golden prompt set, so we need that from Maya.
[00:40:20] Maya: what about cost accounting? if we route to soft-fallback, how will that show up in per-route token costs in the console?
[00:40:27] Priya: billing attribution will show per-route and per-model breakdowns; soft-fallback traffic will show as a separate route and cost. we'll also add a token-level delta so you can estimate marginal cost of each routing decision.
[00:40:39] Rita: one more thing — for compliance we need immutable audit logs for model version changes and who initiated them.
[00:40:45] Marcus: that's in the plan: every change emits an audit event, with user, timestamp, oldVersion->newVersion, and a signed event captured to your SIEM if you want. some customers asked if we can export to their Splunk/ELK.
[00:40:58] Shawn: please include the event schema so infra can validate.
[00:41:02] Marcus: will do.
[00:41:05] [00:48:00] Lena: quick recap of agreements — Brightpath provides 100 eval prompts (due 03/08), Redwood runs latency and p95 sweep (due 03/09), SE authors failover playbook (due 03/10), Lena shares pricing and commit options (due 03/07).
[00:48:20] Daniel: sounds good. small ask — can we get a short runbook version for execs (one page) and a more detailed runbook for SRE?
[00:48:28] Lena: yes we'll craft both; exec one-pager and SRE checklist.
[00:48:35] Maya: i'll also try to run a staging SSO test this week and report back.
[00:48:40] Shawn: and i'll confirm the KMS rotation window and required audit events.
[00:48:45] Lena: perfect, thanks everyone. we'll circulate meeting notes and action items.
[00:49:00] [00:51:30] Lena: any final q's?
[00:51:35] Daniel: nope, thanks.
[00:51:40] Maya: thanks all.
[00:51:45] Lena: bye everyone.
